statement.p: Find the length of the curve x = -\left(5+t\right),\quad y = 3-5t, z = 4+2t, for 2 \le t \le 4.

p.em: (Think of second way that you could calculate this length, too, and see that you get the same result.)

static.solution: \hbox{Length} = \int_2^4 \sqrt{(x'(t))^2 + (y'(t))^2 + (z'(t))^2}\,dt = \int_{2}^{4} \sqrt{(-1)^2+(-5)^2+(2)^2}\,dt = 2\sqrt{30}. This is the length of a straight line from the point (-7,-7,8) to (-9,-17,12).
